evidence.paraphrase: Brahmā turns from the festival account to the goddess’s reappearance: she had hidden from fear and learns the daitya’s death from Śiva. The world-mother emerges at a Himalayan cave mouth, sees a forested mountain with lions/tigers/deer, and laments separation. She asks the omniscient Śiva why he does not recognize her alone, wonders when she will see him, and calls her father for shelter. She asks him to consider her newly emerged from his belly again, reunite her with Śiva and quickly seek that husband; otherwise she threatens to abandon her body from the cliff.
evidence.verification_notes: Direct Sanskrit body reading; not independent edition verification. Uncertain Sanskrit clauses identified separately.

evidence.paraphrase: An unnamed dhīvara hears the weeping girl and reports to Himavat. He describes a beautifully adorned young woman: sun-like ear ornaments, jeweled crown, sixteen-pearl forehead ornament, jeweled hair flower/pearl strands, nose ornament, armlets/bangles/rings, pearl necklace, jeweled waist girdle, cloth, golden ankle chains and sounding anklets/toe ornaments. When seen and questioned she does not answer him but repeats Himavat’s name.
evidence.verification_notes: Direct Sanskrit body reading; not independent edition verification. Uncertain Sanskrit clauses identified separately.

evidence.paraphrase: Himavat hastens to his daughter and consoles her. He addresses her as origin of creation/maintenance/end, possessing all powers and wishes and present inside living beings, able to act, refrain or act otherwise. He says she is never separate from Śiva, yet promises to bring about the union she seeks. Taking her to his own home, he tells her to rise; Pārvatī rejoices on seeing Menā with sons.
evidence.verification_notes: Direct Sanskrit body reading; not independent edition verification. Uncertain Sanskrit clauses identified separately.

evidence.paraphrase: Still sighing and eager to see Śiva, she bows to her father and asks for an effective vow, gift or arduous tapas, offering to perform severe austerity as previously. Himavat considers and recommends worship of Vighnarāja that gives the four goals and obtains Śiva. He cites earlier practice by Mahendra and other gods and Nārada’s sages, leading to attainments such as Indra’s office.

evidence.paraphrase: Himavat says Gaṇeśa granted Brahmā creation-capacity, Viṣṇu protection-capacity, Śiva firm destruction-capacity, and Śeṣa earth-supporting capacity. narrative_events.details: Pārvatī says she does not know a mantra and asks Himavat to teach it for Gaṇeśa favour and Śiva attainment. He says Gaṇeśa has countless varied-success mantras. Lotus-seat, sense restraint and nyāsa precede chosen japa. One-syllable mantra receives one lakh or half-lakh; six-syllable receives niyuta or ayuta; five/ten/eight-syllable practices are mentioned, and28-letter mantra receives ayuta count. These practices seek the practitioner’s own desired attainments.
narrative_events.outcome: Mantra classes and counts taught; syllabic lengths are not invented mantra strings.

narrative_events.cause: General mantra options become a personal instruction.
narrative_events.details: Himavat specifically offers Pārvatī the excellent one-syllable and six-letter mantras, commands beginning on bright fourth of Nabhas, and prescribes a month-long undertaking. He predicts she will certainly obtain Śiva and any other desired object.
narrative_events.outcome: Pārvatī receives explicit instructor/date/duration and promised reunion, not yet its enactment.

narrative_events.cause: Month vow receives expanded beneficiary/result scale.
narrative_events.details: Himavat gives an image-number scale available to women and men:1earthen image yields wishes/wealth/sons/livestock;2makes the impossible attainable;3kingdom/jewels/prosperity;4four goals;5universal kingship;6creation/maintenance/end capacity;7/8/9omniscience of past/present/future. Ten-image worship makes33crore gods including Fire/Indra/Śiva/Viṣṇu and Sanaka’s sages serve;11gives mastery over the printed ten Rudras;12gives12Āditya dominion. Increase worship in severe crises up to108to gain respective fruits; daily lakh worship yields great liberation.
narrative_events.outcome: Every enumerated count/result preserved, including unusual ten-Rudra wording without harmonization.

narrative_events.cause: General scale is supplemented with timed targeted practices.
narrative_events.details: The prisoner desiring release should have5images made and is promised release after3×7nights through Gaṇeśa favour. Devoted person’s7images daily for5years remove great sin. Lifelong worship of1earthen image makes the person identified with Gaṇeśa and obstacle-removing through being seen; one should worship that person for wishes, as the deity is said to be more pleased by this devotee worship than his own. Three images worshipped9days remove all illness/suffering. Gold,silver,copper,rītikā,bronze,pearl/coral images yield the same stated fruits.
narrative_events.outcome: Release, long-practice sin relief, devotee worship and illness relief conditions stated.

narrative_events.cause: Month practice reaches the prescribed festival date.
narrative_events.details: Himavat affirms all wishes through the vow continued until Bhādrapada’s fourth. That day requires a festival according to resources and a night vigil with stories,music,song. Next dawn, clean bathing and previous-style Varada Gaṇeśa worship precede homa in a properly formed pit or ground altar, offerings1/10ofjapa, full oblation preceded by bali.
narrative_events.outcome: Festival,vigil and japa-to-homa ratio specified in source sequence.

narrative_events.cause: Homa leads into teacher honour,tarpana and communal gifts.
narrative_events.details: Worship the ācārya with cows,land,garments,wealth etc., satisfy Brahmins and complete remaining homa. Tarpana is1/10of preceding amount and feeding Veda-knowing Brahmins with their wives1/10of that; give ornaments,cloth and feasible dakṣiṇā, and women’s ornaments/blouses. Conduct all according to means without financial deceit for pleasure of Gaṇanātha with Siddhi and Buddhi.
narrative_events.outcome: Ratios,teacher/community recipients and resources/financial-honesty condition explicit.

narrative_events.cause: Feeding/gifts close solemn observance; immersion follows next day.
narrative_events.details: Eat respectfully with friends. On the following day place the image on a human-carried conveyance decorated with parasol,flags,banners and fly-whisks, with young men performing staff combat in front. Go to a large reservoir, immerse the image in water, and return home amid instruments/song.
narrative_events.outcome: Complete taught vow procedure closes at immersion/home return; Pārvatī’s actual observance/reunion not yet narrated.
